value.overview: The Yellow Warbler (Setophaga petechia) is a warbler recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from bright yellow warbler body, fine reddish streaks on breeding males, rounded head, plain wings, and active foraging in willows or wet thickets. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 49 state or DC summaries, including AK, AL, AR, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, GA, IA, ID, IL, IN, and 35 more. It is most associated with Forests:  Temperate Generalist and Wetlands:  Generalist, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Yellow Warbler belongs to the family New World Warblers in the order Passeriformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for bright yellow warbler body, fine reddish streaks on breeding males, rounded head, plain wings, and active foraging in willows or wet thickets. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
